result.rationale: In the diff, the handler compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Node's IncomingHttpHeaders values can be `string[]`, in which case the strict inequality always fails and valid requests are rejected (and conversely the comparison is fragile against misconfiguration since no startup validation of the secret exists). This is a plausible, diff-grounded correctness/auth-handling defect; the exact impact of the empty-secret scenario is partially mitigated by the APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gate in constants.

adjudication.rationale: The handler is gated by `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (packages/lib/constants.ts), which is only truthy when both `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are set to truthy (non-empty) strings. If the secret is the empty-string default from `.env.example`, the endpoint returns 403 (“not enabled”) before any header comparison, so misconfiguration does not “weaken auth silently” per the diff. Also, while `req.headers[...]` can be `string | string[] | undefined`, comparing a `string[]` to the secret would fail closed (403), not weaken authentication.
